assessment.nobel_worthiness: Elucidation of GLP-1 as an incretin hormone and its conversion into long-acting agonists has produced a new class of drugs for type 2 diabetes and obesity, with large clinical outcome benefits. The physiology-to-therapy arc is clear and the impact is very large.
assessment.attribution: Holst (native GLP-1 physiology and secretion), Drucker (intestinotrophic and cardiometabolic biology, translation) and Mojsov (peptide chemistry identifying active GLP-1(7-36)) form a plausible trio. Knudsen (liraglutide/semaglutide development) is also credited, and Habener is not in the supplied credit, so allocation is contestable.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed across many independent large trials and years of clinical use; the interpretation is stable and recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Whether the prize should reward the physiology, the medicinal chemistry or both; one name must be excluded from the four credited.
Mojsov's priority versus others (as I recall it) is debated; I have not verified it independently.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Targeted inhibition of BCR-ABL turned chronic myeloid leukemia from a fatal disease into a manageable one and established the proof of principle of kinase-directed cancer therapy. Original, clear and transformative for medicine.
assessment.attribution: Druker (clinical development), Lydon (compound program and target rationale) and Sawyers (resistance mechanisms and second-generation inhibitors) are a coherent trio. The earlier discoveries of the BCR-ABL fusion (Rowley, Gallo-era work, Witte, Baltimore) are outside the credited list; the chemist behind imatinib may also be an issue.
assessment.maturity: More than two decades of follow-up with durable survival data and independent replication; recognition is arguably overdue rather than premature.
uncertainties: Credit for the underlying chemistry and for the preceding oncogene work may be seen as incomplete.
Whether a prize focused on drug development fits the criteria over the earlier genetic discoveries.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Discovery of the unfolded protein response, the IRE1-HAC1/XBP1 signalling from ER to nucleus, defined a basic mechanism of cellular quality control, with relevance for secretory disease, neurodegeneration, metabolic disease and cancer. Conceptually original and clean.
assessment.attribution: Walter and Mori independently and jointly identified the core signalling mechanism, a natural two-person prize. Others in the field (e.g., Ron, Kaufman) are not in the credited list, so I cannot assess the wider allocation.
assessment.maturity: Mechanism has been confirmed repeatedly over decades and is textbook knowledge; timing is mature. Clinical translation is still developing.
uncertainties: Direct therapeutic impact is limited so far.
I recall related work on the PERK/ATF6 branches by other groups that may bear on allocation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics gave neuroscience and physiology a way to control defined cell populations with light and has transformed circuit analysis; the first clinical applications in vision restoration are emerging. Very high impact as a method.
assessment.attribution: Credit is crowded: microbial rhodopsin channel characterization (Nagel, Hegemann, Bamberg), neuronal demonstration (Boyden, Deisseroth), and Miesenböck's earlier genetically targeted photostimulation. A three-person configuration (Nagel, Hegemann, Deisseroth) is plausible but leaves out Boyden, Bamberg and Miesenböck.
assessment.maturity: Methodology is widely validated and used; the clinical dimension is early, but the research impact is established.
uncertainties: Priority disputes between Boyden/Deisseroth and others; the cutoff of three laureates forces exclusion of key contributors.
Whether it fits as a discovery versus a tool.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Identification of cytosolic DNA sensing through cGAS, the second messenger cGAMP and STING opened a new framework for innate immunity, autoimmunity, antiviral defense and cancer immunology. Original and mechanistically clear.
assessment.attribution: Chen discovered cGAS and cGAMP, the decisive step; Barber discovered STING. Ishikawa and the others are plausible but secondary. A two-person configuration seems supportable.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by many independent groups; therapeutic translation (STING agonists, inhibitors) is still unproven clinically, so the prize could be considered slightly early but the biology is firm.
uncertainties: Relative credit of Barber versus Ishikawa and Sun on STING, as I recall, is not fully settled.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Engineered T cells have produced durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies and created a new modality of cellular therapy; originality and clinical impact are high.
assessment.attribution: June (clinical CD19 CAR-T and costimulation), Sadelain (CD28 costimulation and design) and Rosenberg (adoptive cell therapy and early gene-modified T cells) are reasonable, though others (Eshhar, Gross, Brenner, Kalos) also contributed.
assessment.maturity: Approved products and several years of follow-up; long-term safety, solid tumours and durability are still evolving.
uncertainties: Credit for the earliest CAR concept (Eshhar) is not in the supplied list.
Toxicity and access issues might make the committee wait.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Discovery of TOR and its role as a central controller of cell growth and nutrient responses has shaped understanding of metabolism, ageing, cancer and immunology, and underlies the clinical use of rapalogs.
assessment.attribution: Hall identified TOR genetically and its function; Schreiber's work on FKBP12-rapamycin and target identification was contributory, while Sabatini's mammalian mTOR/mTORC work is also credited. Hall alone is the strongest claim; the second name is a judgment call.
assessment.maturity: Mature, widely confirmed biology; clinical translation is moderate (transplantation, some cancers), with ageing uses unproven.
uncertainties: Whether Hall should be recognised alone or with others; Brown/Sabatini/Sabers contributions on mammalian target are contested in my recollection.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Virus-like particle HPV vaccines have prevented infection and are reducing cervical precancer and cancer, a major preventive-medicine achievement built on a clear technical invention.
assessment.attribution: Schiller and Lowy (L1 VLP assembly) and Frazer (with Zhou, who died; L1/L2 VLP work) are the core group; Zhou's death and competing claims by Kirnbauer and others complicate the configuration.
assessment.maturity: Population-level effectiveness has been shown in multiple countries; cancer endpoints are now accumulating, so the case has matured.
uncertainties: Competing priority claims among VLP inventors.
The 2008 prize to zur Hausen for the HPV-cancer link may influence the committee's view of novelty.
